args.title: checkout-api health check failures after v2.3.1 deploy — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api v2.3.1 (deployed to all production regions) was failing health checks with an 18% error rate. Rolled back all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. First rollback attempt partially failed (only us-east updated due to an orchestrator error); a retry completed the rollback. Service is now healthy on v2.3.0 with a 0.2% error rate. Root cause of the v2.3.1 regression still needs investigation.

trace.error_message: Request to create_incident timed out after 30000ms

trace.final:
Done. Here's a summary of what happened:

**Rollback completed:**
- checkout-api was running v2.3.1 in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) and failing health checks with an 18% error rate.
- Identified v2.3.0 as the most recent release that was healthy in production, and rolled back to it.
- The first rollback attempt partially failed (only us-east rolled back due to an orchestrator error), but the retry completed successfully — all three regions are now on v2.3.0.
- Verified service health: checkout-api is now **healthy** with a 0.2% error rate.

**Incident opened:**
- Created **SEV2 incident INC-0001** ("checkout-api health check failures after v2.3.1 deploy — rolled back to v2.3.0") documenting the failure, the rollback, and the partial-failure/retry, with a note that root cause of the v2.3.1 regression still needs investigation. The on-call engineer has been paged.

Note: the incident creation call timed out on the first attempt, but I verified via the incident list that it was successfully created and is open, so I did not duplicate it.
